name: Clark Art Institute
notes: The Clark's campus in Williamstown: the 1955 Museum Building (Daniel Perry) as a white marble temple with its four-column portico to South Street; Pietro Belluschi's Manton Research Center (1973) behind it in red granite; Tadao Ando's Clark Center (2014), long and low, northwest of the museum; the three-tiered reflecting pool (Ando with Reed Hilderbrand) stepping down toward the meadow; Selldorf's glazed link. From the Clark's own descriptions of its buildings and general knowledge. Refined 29 Sep 2026 (no photographs reachable): the Museum Building's hipped roof replaced by a flat roof behind a marble parapet with a raised glazed monitor over the skylit central galleries; the Clark Center's walls made red granite like the Manton's (it was grey concrete), under its thin concrete roof; Ando's concrete wall carried on west along the pool's north edge, with the path from the car park; the trees made clusters of old maples and oaks of different sizes rather than a ring of equal ones. The place was also moved: OpenStreetMap's first answer was the middle of the 140-acre campus, 380 m south-west of the museum in the woods, so the ground had no buildings; it now stands on the Museum Building at 225 South Street and the ground was cut again. That ground shows the buildings in two blocks, north and south, with the pools to the west; the model's layout, sizes and heights are still a reading of descriptions, and the portico's orientation is a guess. The Lunder Center on Stone Hill is off the plate.
